name: DM_BC6H_RGB9E5
meaning: `=1` decodes BC6H (HDR) textures into RGB9E5Float, 4 bytes per pixel, instead of RGBA16Float, 8 bytes, when the BC textures are decoded on the CPU (profile `tex_bc_cpu` on a GPU without BC support): half the memory, negative values become 0 and each colour keeps 9 bits of mantissa. Off by default. The launcher's Downsample HDR textures sets it

name: DM_CHAIN_INDEX
meaning: `=<index>` appends `_<index>` to the default shell framework name (`DmGame<title ID>_<index>`) and its Objective-C/Swift namespace tag in `build_ipa.sh` when building chained NRO sub-frameworks for the shared shell

name: DM_CURSOR_HIDDEN
meaning: `=1` (Mac) starts the game with the pointer already hidden, as the launcher sets it when its console had hidden the pointer, so it does not show up for a moment between the two windows. The usual rule of `DM_CURSOR_HIDE` takes over once the pointer is over the game window

name: DM_CURSOR_HIDE
meaning: `=<seconds>` hides the Mac pointer after that many seconds without movement over the game window (3 by default) and shows it again on the next movement, click or scroll; `0` keeps it

name: DM_EXPERIMENTAL_BUILDER
meaning: `1` makes the NSP script run the extraction and the shader split through nxbuild's binaries beside `NXB_BIN` (the path of its `nxb` binary) where nxbuild supports the case, with the same outputs; any other case, an unsupported stage or an output that fails the checks runs the standard way (the Mac launcher's Use experimental builder setting)

name: DM_FOCUS_KEEP
meaning: On by default: the game stays in focus while its Mac window is up, whichever app is active (minimizing still counts). `=0` sends focus changes when another app takes the key window; `scripts/regress.py` sets it, so another app taking the key window during a run does not pause a game that stops out of focus

name: DM_FORK_PATCHES
meaning: the fork patches a build carries, comma separated (build_ipa.sh and build_shell.sh read dm/fork_patches.txt into it): `DMForkPatches` in the app's Info.plist and the first log line

name: DM_FRAMEWORK
meaning: `=1` (route C M1) compiles the game's modules into `DmIOS.app/Frameworks/DmGame.framework` instead of the executable, which `dlopen`s it at launch (`dm/ios/project-framework.yml`; the NSP script's `--framework` sets it); the default 0 keeps the usual in-executable build

name: DM_FRAMEWORK_NAME
meaning: `=<name>` overrides the game framework product name (`FW_NAME`) in `build_ipa.sh` (default `DmGame`, or `DmGame<title ID>` with `DM_FRAMEWORK_ONLY`)

name: DM_FRAMEWORK_ONLY
meaning: `=<folder>` (route C shell) makes build_ipa.sh build only the game's framework, `<folder>/DmGame<title ID>.framework` with its shader libraries, pipeline archive, settings list and icon, unsigned, for build_shell.sh (the NSP script's `--shell-framework` sets it)

name: DM_FULL_ROMFS
meaning: `=1` in `build_ipa.sh` packs the game data into the IPA as it did before the slim package; the default leaves it in `Documents/games/<id>/` (`romfs.img`, `aoc/<index>.img`) and the DLC beside it. Only for small games — a full package of a large one is many GB and iOS refuses it (`PackageExtractionFailed`)

name: DM_GAME_MENU_TEXT
meaning: The iOS in-game menu's own words in the player's language, one per line: the menu's title (more settings on the start screen), Controller layout, Keys that toggle and None (GameMenu.swift). A missing or empty line stays English. The shell passes it at launch, a game's own app gets it in its bundled `dm/env.txt` with the lines joined by `\n`

name: DM_HOME_MENU
meaning: `0` turns off the Mac's Home menu (on by default): a short press of the controller's Home button opens it over the paused game, with Resume, Back to console mode (only with `DM_HOME_MENU_LAUNCHER=1`) and Quit (which opens the quit prompt), up and down choose, A selects, B or Home resumes (`home_quit.h`, `home_quit_mac.h`)

name: DM_HOME_MENU_LAUNCHER
meaning: `1`: the Mac's Home menu has Back to console mode, which pauses the game in the background (as a minimized window), hides it and activates the launcher (`DM_LAUNCHER_BUNDLE_ID`). It resumes when it is active again or on the distributed notification `org.nxnative.resume.<pid>`, quits on `org.nxnative.quit.<pid>`, and posts `org.nxnative.paused.<pid>` and `org.nxnative.resumed.<pid>`. A front end such as NX2Apple sets it for a game started from its console mode ([Starting a game](frontends.md#starting-a-game))

name: DM_HOME_QUIT
meaning: `0` turns off quitting with the controller's Home button (Mac and iOS, on by default): held for 2 s it opens a quit prompt over the game, A quits as ⌘Q does (on iOS the app closes after the cloud saves went out, as Quit in the in-game menu does), B or Home closes it (`home_quit.h`, `quit_prompt.h`)

name: DM_HOME_QUIT_TEXT
meaning: The texts of the Home button's quit prompt and Home menu in the player's language, one per line: the hold indicator, the title, the note, the quit and the cancel button, then the menu's Resume, its Back to console mode and its title (the game's name). A front end such as NX2Apple sets it ([Starting a game](frontends.md#starting-a-game)), an empty or missing line keeps the English text

name: DM_HUD_PER_LAYER
meaning: `1`: the shell app sets it at start together with `MTL_HUD_ENABLED`, and the game view then turns Apple's Metal HUD off on its layer unless `DM_METAL_HUD` is `1`

name: DM_JOYCON_SPLIT
meaning: Bluetooth Nintendo Switch Joy-Con (L/R) on macOS (`0x057e:0x2006` and `0x057e:0x2007`) over `IOHIDManager` (`pad_joycon_mac.h`, on by default; `0` falls back to GameController, `1` starts split into two sideways player slots instead of paired on one slot with SL+SR / L+R 3 s hold switching)

name: DM_KEYMAP
meaning: Mac keyboard: `<name>=<key code>,…` puts a button (`A` … `Down`), a stick direction (`LUp` … `RRight`) or `Shake` on another key (macOS virtual key code, or `none`); one key holds one function (`input_map.h`); a Mac app also keeps it as the saved choice `launcher.DM_KEYMAP`, used when the host takes the whole value

name: DM_LAUNCHER_BUNDLE_ID
meaning: `=<bundle id>`: the launcher the Mac's Home menu shows on Back to console mode (`DM_HOME_MENU_LAUNCHER`): the game hands it the activation before it hides, and opens it when it is not running. Unset, macOS shows the app behind the game

name: DM_NS_TAG
meaning: `=<tag>` overrides the per-framework Objective-C class and Swift module namespace tag (`DmFw_<tag>_*` and `DmGame_<tag>`) passed to `gen_objc_namespace.py` and `xcodebuild` in `build_ipa.sh`

name: DM_PAD_MAP
meaning: Mac controllers: `<name>=<name>,…` makes the button that sends the first by default send the second (or `none` / `Shake`), e.g. `A=B,B=A` swaps them (`input_map.h`); a Mac app also keeps it as the saved choice `launcher.DM_PAD_MAP`, used when the host takes the whole value

name: DM_PREFLIGHT
meaning: Set: a Mac app exits at once with status 0, before it reads its Info.plist, rolls its log or touches the saves, so a front end can open a new build through LaunchServices and macOS runs its first-start check of the bundle then (`launcher.c`, docs/frontends.md)

name: DM_PROFILE
meaning: `=<file>`: the runtime game profile (layout, switches, tables) the host reads at start, which is how one host binary serves every game (the launcher architecture); the compiled `game_profile.h` stays the fallback, and `DM_PROF_<key>` overrides sit on top of it (`hle_profile.h`)

name: DM_SCREEN
meaning: `=<number>` opens the Mac window on the connected screen with that `NSScreenNumber` (`CGDirectDisplayID`), centred, before any `DM_FULLSCREEN` request; an unknown number is logged and ignored. The NX2Apple launcher sets it to its own window's screen

name: DM_STEAM_DEADZONE
meaning: `=0..0.9` (exclusive upper bound) sets the radial deadzone for both raw Steam Controller sticks; default 0.10, `0` disables it; invalid values use the default

name: DM_STEAM_HID
meaning: `=0` disables the Mac direct Steam Controller HID adapter and leaves input to Apple GameController; enabled otherwise

name: DM_STICK_DEADZONE_L
meaning: `=1..50` sets a radial deadzone of that many percent of the travel for the left stick of every physical controller (inside it the stick reads centred, outside it the rest of the travel is rescaled to the full range); unset, `0` or anything else leaves the stick as the controller reports it. The Mac launcher's Controls settings write it (Use custom deadzones)

name: DM_STICK_DEADZONE_R
meaning: `=1..50` the same for the right stick

name: DM_TOUCH_HINT
meaning: Localized words for the iOS right-stick hint, shown once per launch when the 3D layout has room and no controller is connected. Empty disables the hint

name: DM_TOUCH_LAYOUT
meaning: The player's per-layout touch-control arrangement, encoded by the shell's touch layout editor. Invalid values keep the built-in positions

name: DM_TOUCH_SIZE
meaning: iOS touch-control size: small, medium (default) or large. Controls move toward medium when the requested size does not fit

name: DM_TOUCH_STICK
meaning: iOS left touch-stick position: corner (default), higher or inward

name: DM_TOUCH_TOGGLE
meaning: iOS touch keys set to Toggle in the shell's touch layout editor, as control names joined by commas (for example `zl,zr,a`): a tap turns the key on, the next tap off. Also set by the in-game menu of a game's own app (the Touch keys that toggle row), which has no layout editor. Unset, every key is held

name: DM_UI_HOLD
meaning: When set, keeps the controller mapping test window open for 60 seconds after its UI screenshot for manual inspection
